exam: 2023年3月 第1套 · 仔细阅读 P1
title: It's good to be smart.…

sents.en: It's good to be smart.
After all, intelligent people earn more money, accumulate more wealth, and even live longer.
sents.cn: 毕竟，聪明人赚更多钱、积累更多财富，甚至活得更久。

sents.en: But there's another side to the story.
The brightest people and strongest leaders sometimes make errors others don't, especially in situations that require common sense.
sents.cn: 最聪明的人和最强力的领导者有时会犯别人不会犯的错，尤其是在需要常识的情境下。

sents.en: Travis Bradberry, president at TalentSmart, explained Bradberry in his post Why Smart People Act so Stupid that "rational thinking and intelligence don't tend to go hand in hand".
sents.cn: TalentSmart总裁TravisBradberry在他《聪明人为何如此愚蠢地行事》一文中解释道，"理性思维与智力往往并不携手而行"。

sents.en: Intelligent people are more prone to silly mistakes because of blind spots in how they use logic.
sents.cn: 聪明人更容易犯愚蠢的错误，因为他们运用逻辑的方式存在盲点。

sents.en: These blind spots exist because smart people tend to be overconfident in their reasoning abilities.
sents.cn: 这些盲点的存在，是因为聪明人往往对自己的推理能力过于自信。

sents.en: "They're so used to being right and having quick answers that they don't even realise when they're making a mess by answering without thinking things through."
sents.cn: "他们太习惯于正确、习惯于快速给出答案，以至于在未经思考就作答、把事情搞砸时，他们甚至毫无察觉。"

sents.en: A lifetime of praise leads smart people to develop too much faith in their intelligence and abilities.
sents.cn: 一生的赞美让聪明人对自己的智力和能力产生了过度的自信。

sents.en: They often fail to recognise when they need help, and when they do recognise it, they tend to believe that no one else is capable of providing it.
sents.cn: 他们常常意识不到自己何时需要帮助；而即便意识到了，也往往认为别人没有能力提供帮助。

sents.en: "It's hard for anyone to graciously accept the fact that they're wrong.
sents.cn: "任何人都要优雅地接受自己犯错的事实都不容易。

sents.en: It's even harder for smart people because they grow so used to being right all the time that it becomes a part of their identity," Bradberry wrote.
sents.cn: 对聪明人而言更难，因为他们太习惯于始终正确，以至于这成了他们身份的一部分，"Bradberry写道，"对聪明人来说，犯错可能像是一种人身攻击，而正确则成了一种必需。

sents.en: "For smart people, being wrong can feel like a personal attack, and being right, a necessity."
Smart people also have a hard time accepting feedback.
sents.cn: 聪明人也很难接受反馈。

sents.en: They tend to undervalue the opinions of others, which means they have trouble believing that anyone is qualified to give them useful feedback.
sents.cn: 他们往往低估他人的意见，这意味着他们难以相信有人有资格给他们提供有用的反馈。

sents.en: Not only does this tendency hinder their growth and performance, it can lead to harmful relationships, both personally and professionally.
sents.cn: 这种倾向不仅阻碍他们的成长与表现，还可能导致有害的人际关系——无论私人还是职场。

sents.en: Smart people develop overachieving personalities because things come so easily to them.
sents.cn: 聪明人之所以形成"过度成就"的性格，是因为事情对他们来说太容易了。

sents.en: They simply don't understand how hard some people have to work to accomplish the same things, and because of that, they push people too hard.
sents.cn: 他们根本不理解有些人要付出多大努力才能完成同样的事，正因如此，他们把别人逼得太紧。

sents.en: They set the bar too high, and when people take too long or don't get things quite right, they assume it's due to a lack of effort.
sents.cn: 他们把标准定得太高，而当别人花太久或做得不够好时，他们就认为是努力不够。

sents.en: So they push even harder.
